Hi everyone! 👋  My name's Alex, and I'm thrilled to finally join this community.  I'm a wheelchair user, diagnosed with Spina Bifida at birth.  For those unfamiliar, it's a neural tube defect that affects the development of the spine and spinal cord, resulting in varying degrees of paralysis.  For me, it means I navigate the world from a chair.
It hasn't always been easy. Growing up, accessibility wasn't always a priority.  Remember those childhood memories of running and playing?  I had to find different ways to participate, to adapt.  That often meant watching from the sidelines, which stung sometimes, but it also pushed me to discover my own strength and resilience.  I learned to climb trees (a modified version, of course!), to find creative solutions to everyday obstacles, and to appreciate the people who helped me reach those seemingly impossible branches.
My life isn't defined by my disability, though.  I'm a writer, a passionate advocate for accessibility, and a lover of all things outdoors (my adapted mountain bike is my pride and joy!). I'm also incredibly clumsy, prone to spilling coffee and bumping into things – a running joke amongst my friends.  
I'm joining this platform to connect with others who understand the everyday realities of living with a disability. To share stories, to laugh, to learn, and maybe even inspire a little bit of change along the way. I want to challenge perceptions, celebrate our strengths, and advocate for a more inclusive world.  
So, hello!  Looking forward to getting to know you all.  Feel free to ask me anything – no question is too silly or too personal.  Let's build a supportive and understanding space together. #SpinaBifida #WheelchairUser #DisabilityPride #AccessibilityMatters #Inclusion #DisabilityAdvocacy

Hi everyone! 👋  My name's Alex, and I'm thrilled to finally be joining this community.  I'm a 28-year-old artist and writer, and I live with cerebral palsy.  This means my movement isn't always as easy or straightforward as most people experience.  It's a part of who I am, but it’s not *all* of who I am.
For a long time, I felt a lot of pressure to "hide" my disability.  Like, if I could just be "normal" enough, people would treat me "normally." That's a tiring, and frankly, pretty inaccurate way to live.  I've learned that the "normal" is just a spectrum, and everyone has their own set of challenges and triumphs.
My CP affects my coordination and balance mostly.  Simple tasks like writing for extended periods or carrying things can be challenging, requiring extra time and effort.  Navigating crowded spaces can be a sensory overload, and sometimes I need extra help. I use a cane for stability, and I'm pretty darn good at adapting!  
One of the hardest things about living with a disability is the constant negotiation. Negotiating accessibility, negotiating assumptions, negotiating patience and understanding.  It can be exhausting! But I'm also fiercely independent, and I've found incredibly creative ways to work around the limitations.  That’s partly what fuels my art – finding beauty and expression even when things aren't easy.
I'm joining this platform to connect with others, share my experiences, and maybe even inspire a little bit of empathy and understanding.  I'm hoping to share my art, my writing, and stories about navigating the world with a disability.  I'm excited to learn from you all too!  
So, hello!  Let's chat. What's your favorite way to overcome a challenge?  #CerebralPalsy #DisabilityPride #Accessibility #RepresentationMatters #Artist #Writer #AdaptiveLife

I'm making this post because I want to share a bit about myself and my experience with autism. It's something that's a huge part of who I am, and I'm hoping to connect with others who understand or are curious to learn more.
For me, autism manifests in a few key ways.  Sensory sensitivities are a big one – loud noises can be incredibly overwhelming, and certain textures make me incredibly uncomfortable.  Bright lights are also a challenge.  I often need quiet time to recharge after social situations, even if I enjoyed them.  It's not that I *don't* like people, it's that social interactions require a lot of energy from me.
Communication can sometimes be tricky too. I sometimes struggle to understand unspoken social cues or sarcasm, and I can find it difficult to express myself fully, especially when feeling stressed or overwhelmed. I’ve learned strategies to help, like practicing active listening and using visual aids to communicate my needs.
One thing that's really important to me is routine and predictability.  Changes to my schedule can be really anxiety-inducing, so I plan things out carefully to minimize unexpected disruptions.  This helps me feel safe and secure.
I'm not going to lie, navigating the world as an autistic person has its challenges. There are times when I feel misunderstood, or even judged for my differences. But I'm also incredibly proud of who I am.  My autism gives me unique perspectives and talents – I'm highly detail-oriented, I have a strong capacity for focus when I'm engaged in something I'm passionate about, and I see the world in a way many others don't.
I'm hoping to use this platform to share my experiences, advocate for autistic rights, and connect with other autistic individuals and allies.  If you're autistic, feel free to reach out – I'd love to hear your story!  And if you're not autistic, I'm happy to answer any questions you have, respectfully of course.  Let's work together to create a more inclusive and understanding world.  #autism #autismawareness #neurodiversity #autisticadvocacy #myautismstory

Today was… a beige day.  Everything felt muted, like I was watching the world through a dirty window.  The usual stuff – woke up feeling heavy, like a lead weight was strapped to my chest.  Tried to get ready for work, but the simplest tasks felt monumental.  Showering?  A Herculean effort.  Choosing clothes?  An impossible decision.
At work, I felt like a ghost.  People talked *around* me, not *to* me.  I couldn't quite focus, my mind flitting between anxieties I couldn't quite name and memories I didn't want to revisit.  Lunch was just… sad.  A sad sandwich.  A beige sandwich.
The drive home felt endless.  Each traffic light felt like a tiny victory, and each red light a crushing defeat.  Now I'm home, and the silence is deafening.  It's not a peaceful silence; it's a heavy, suffocating silence.
I know this isn't the most upbeat post, but sometimes… sometimes it's all I've got.  It's the truth of my day.  I'm fighting.  I'm trying.  But some days, the fight feels… small.  And beige.
If anyone else is feeling the beige today, you're not alone.  Sending you a virtual hug (if you want one).  And maybe… maybe tomorrow will be a slightly less beige day.  🤞
#depression #mentalhealth #beigemood #youarenotalone #itsokaytonotbeokay

The sun's shining, which is ironic, considering my internal weather forecast calls for thunderstorms and torrential downpours of apathy.  Saw a few people laughing in the park earlier.  Sounded... loud.  Annoying even.  Probably not fair, but that's depression for you, I guess.  It makes you selfish.  It makes everything selfish.
Work was... work.  The kind of beige, soul-crushing work that makes you feel like you’re slowly being sucked into a vacuum cleaner of motivation.  Managed to get through, though.  Small victories, right?  Even if the victory feels more like surviving than thriving.
Later, I'm gonna try to force myself to eat something.  Probably toast.  It's reliable.  It doesn't judge my inability to feel joy.  Then, maybe, maybe I'll try to read a book.  Or maybe I'll just stare at the ceiling until sleep claims me.  We'll see how the internal battle goes.
If anyone else out there is feeling similarly… lost in the fog, adrift in a sea of blah… know you’re not alone.  Even though it feels like it sometimes.  Sending out a tiny, wavering ray of solidarity into the void.  Maybe it'll find someone who needs it.  Maybe it won't.  Either way, I'm here.  Somewhere.  Probably staring at the ceiling.  Goodnight.  Or good day.  Or… something.
#depression #mentalhealth #itsokaytonotbeokay #justsurviving #smallvictories #feelingblah

column5:
Hey everyone.  Or, hey to the few people who might actually see this.  I'm Alex.  And today… well, today was beige.  Like, the colour beige.  Completely unremarkable.  That's usually how it is, to be honest.
I’m battling depression, which, for those of you who don’t know, isn't just "feeling a bit down."  It's a heavy, suffocating blanket that clings to you all day, every day.  Today the blanket was extra-fluffy, extra-heavy.  The kind that makes even small tasks feel like climbing Everest.  
I didn't get out of bed until noon.  Managed a shower, which felt like an achievement worthy of an Olympic medal.  Made some toast – burnt it, of course.  Perfectly symbolic, really.  
Spent most of the afternoon staring out the window, watching the leaves blow around in the wind.  They seemed so free.  So unburdened.  Envious, much?
I guess the point of this post is… well, I'm not entirely sure.  Maybe it's just to acknowledge that I exist.  That even on days when I feel completely invisible, I'm still here.  Maybe it's a tiny attempt to break through the fog, even if just for a moment.  Maybe it's a plea for connection, a silent hope that someone out there understands.
If you're reading this and you relate, please know you're not alone.  And if you're not, maybe take a moment to think about those who are struggling silently.  Sometimes, just knowing someone sees you is enough.  Even if that "someone" is just a stranger on the internet.
#depression #mentalhealth #invisibleillness #justbeingme #onedayatatime

Hey everyone.  Or, hey to the few people who might actually see this.  I'm Alex.  (Or, you can call me Alex if you want.  It doesn't really matter.)  I'm… well, I'm mostly just existing today.  That's pretty much my superpower these days, existing.
Today was… beige.  Everything felt beige.  The sky, the food I forced myself to eat (toast, again), even the conversation I had with my mom felt beige.  Flat.  Unremarkable.  And exhausting.
I know, I know.  "Beige" is a pretty lame descriptor for a whole day, but it's fitting. It's the color of apathy, right? The color of feeling like nothing really matters and nothing will ever really matter.  That's how depression feels a lot of the time for me.  A heavy, grey beige blanket that just smothers everything.
I managed to get out of bed, which is a win, I guess.  A small, almost insignificant win, but a win nonetheless.  Sometimes those small things are the biggest victories.
I'm posting this because… I don't really know, honestly.  Maybe a little bit of a cry for help, maybe just a way to acknowledge that I'm here, even though it feels like I'm barely existing.  Maybe it's just nice to put words to this feeling, even if no one reads them.
If you're feeling the same way, even a fraction of what I'm feeling, please know you're not alone.  And if you're not, well, thanks for listening.  Even if it's just to a beige post about a beige day.  Maybe tomorrow will be a slightly different shade.  Maybe.
#depression #mentalhealth #beigelife #justexisting #onedayatatime

Hey everyone.  Or, hey, no one.  Both feel equally accurate most days.  I'm Alex, and I'm...well, I'm depressed.  It's not a secret, not really, but it's also not something I usually broadcast.  Today felt... heavy.  Like wearing a lead vest under a wool sweater on a summer day.  You know?  That kind of suffocating.
The sun was shining, supposedly a beautiful day, and everyone seemed to be bustling around, all bright and cheerful.  Meanwhile, I spent most of it staring at a wall, the cheerful chirping of birds sounding more like a mocking chorus.  Went to the grocery store, managed to get some food, but mostly just felt overwhelmed by the bright lights and the sheer *amount* of everything.  Small victories, I guess.
I know people say "get out more," "think positive," and all that. I know. Trust me, I know. It's easier said than done.  It's not a lack of trying; it's a lack of... well, a whole lot of things.  Energy, mostly.  And motivation.  And sometimes, the will to even breathe.
Anyway, just putting it out there.  Maybe someone else feels the same today.  Maybe not. Either way,  sending out a little bit of virtual quiet solidarity to anyone who needs it.  And if you don't need it, well, that's okay too.  Just felt like sharing a sliver of my gray day.  Maybe tomorrow will be brighter.  Maybe.
#depression #mentalhealth #itsokaytonotbeokay #greyday #onedayatatime

Today's been... a day.  The sun was shining, which is supposed to be a good thing, right?  Except the brightness just felt... overwhelming.  Like everything was too much, and nothing at all at the same time.  I spent most of the morning staring at the ceiling, the weight of… well, everything, pressing down.
Then I forced myself to make some tea.  That’s a win, I guess. Small wins. That’s kind of my life motto lately. Small wins and the quiet hum of accepting that some days, the small wins are all I can manage.
Later, I saw a dog park.  Seriously, a small fenced area full of happy dogs.  It was beautiful, truly.  The joy radiating from those furry little chaos-creators was palpable.  It was also a sharp, painful reminder of how little joy I feel right now. The kind of reminder that leaves a hollow ache in your chest.  You know the one.
So, yeah.  That's my day in a nutshell.  Depression, sunshine, tea, and the overwhelming cuteness of dogs. A strange cocktail, really.  Just putting it out there, sharing a little piece of my internal weather report.  If anyone else out there is feeling the same grey skies today, know you're not alone.  Sending virtual hugs (if you want them!).  Maybe tomorrow will be better.  Maybe.
#depression #mentalhealth #itsokaynottobeokay #smallwins #onedayatatime

Hey everyone.  Or, hey to the few who might see this.  I'm Alex.  And… well, today's been… today.  You know?  One of *those* days.
The sun’s shining, apparently. I saw it through the gap in the curtains.  Didn't really register, though.  Feels like it's shining *on* me, not *for* me, if that makes any sense.  It's that kind of muted, grey-behind-the-sunshine kind of day, you know?  The kind that matches my mood perfectly.
Had a conversation with my therapist earlier.  We talked about… well, everything and nothing.  The usual struggle to get out of bed, the lack of motivation, the persistent fog.  It feels like I’m wading through treacle, only the treacle is made of sadness and apathy.
Tried to make myself some toast.  Burnt it.  Figured that was pretty on-brand for the day.
Small victories, I guess.  I got dressed. I brushed my teeth.  Those are things I celebrate, these days.  Tiny, pathetic victories, but victories nonetheless.  It’s the small things, right?  Or maybe that's just what I tell myself to keep going.
If anyone’s out there feeling similarly… know you’re not alone.  Even if it feels like it.  Even if it feels like the whole world is sunshine and you're stuck in the perpetually overcast basement of your own mind.  There's always someone else down here with you.  Maybe we can share some burnt toast.  Maybe.  Later.  Maybe.  
#depression #mentalhealth #itsokaytonotbeokay #smallvictories #burnttoast #onedayatatime

Hey everyone.  Or, uh, hi.  It's... me.  I guess.  I'm usually pretty good at hiding behind the curated perfection of social media, but today... today feels different.  I'm Sarah, and I live with depression.  
It's been a... day.  One of *those* days.  You know the ones.  Where the smallest things feel insurmountable, where the sunlight feels harsh and the quiet feels deafening.  Today, it was the overflowing sink full of dishes that tipped me over the edge.  Seriously.  A sink full of dishes.  I know, it sounds ridiculous.  But today, it felt like a symbol of everything else that's piling up – the unfinished work projects, the unanswered emails, the general sense of being utterly, hopelessly overwhelmed.
I spent most of the afternoon curled up under a blanket, staring at the ceiling.  The usual self-criticism parade marched through my head –  *You're lazy, you're useless, you're a failure.*  The familiar soundtrack of negative self-talk playing on repeat.  
It's not always this bad, obviously. There are days where I function, where I even feel a flicker of something resembling joy. But today isn't one of those days.  And that's okay.  I think.  I'm trying to tell myself that's okay.  It's important to acknowledge these days, the dark days, the days when the weight of everything feels too much.
If you're struggling too, please know you're not alone.  Even if it feels like it.  Even if all you can manage is to breathe.  That's enough.  Sometimes, just breathing is a victory.  Maybe tomorrow will be better.  Maybe not.  But for now, I'm going to try to find some comfort in the quiet darkness.  Goodnight.  Or, good... something.

If you're reading this and feeling similarly… you're not alone.  Really.  Even though it feels like it.  Sometimes just knowing that someone else gets it, even a stranger on the internet, can make a difference.  If you need to talk, DM's are open (though I might not reply instantly – sometimes even typing feels too much).  Just know you’re seen, even if you can’t see yourself right now.  Hang in there.  We'll get through this.  Maybe. One bowl of cereal at a time.
